subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible requests tolerate a generic body `model`, or should the body `model` remain restricted to OpenClaw agent-target values?
rationale: The mechanical code change is small, but it changes a documented public API contract and may need parity across Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

options.title: Adopt Header Precedence
options.body: Treat the valid agent header as authoritative and ignore or tolerate generic body model strings for the endpoint set maintainers choose.

options.title: Preserve Agent-First Model Contract
options.body: Keep rejecting generic body model strings and document that SDK clients should send `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or `openclaw/<agentId>` with optional `x-openclaw-model`.

options.title: Choose Per-Endpoint Semantics
options.body: Limit the change to Chat Completions only and explicitly document why Responses and embeddings keep stricter model validation.

recommendation.title: Adopt Header Precedence
recommendation.body: Treat the valid agent header as authoritative and ignore or tolerate generic body model strings for the endpoint set maintainers choose.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc introduced the current agent-first OpenAI-compatible model contract this issue would change.
